name: Liquid Glass (Digital and 3D Aesthetics; name_en "Liquid Glass"). Explicitly named in the source and not interchangeable with frosted glass. Provenance is explicit.
visualIdentity: Explicit: clear glass boundaries, plausible refraction, edge highlights, and limited dispersion, with a recognizable background visible through the form. Droplets, lenses, or flexible panels animate while deformation and refraction stay continuous. Ordinary translucent blur does not qualify.
suitableUses: Explicit: hero optical moments where refraction is the feature, and device or feature launches that emphasize clarity or optics. Source also cites abstract brand loops and fluid UI concept films as hybrid fits. Inferred: single-lens product framing. Other use cases are unspecified.
limitations: Explicit: text must not sit behind a refracting region, typography stays outside it, and readability and stable boundaries must be preserved. Avoid frosted-blur substitutes, rainbow-heavy dispersion, multiple overlapping lenses, and unbaked chaotic splashing. A 2D approximation must be explicitly labeled as screen-space displacement. Other legibility limits are unspecified.
palette: Reference-dependent example, not intrinsic to the style: background #EDEBE3 (dominant layout), foreground #293C49 (text and hierarchy), accent #91ACB0 (subordinate). Gradients are disabled and tokens are discrete. Contrast: foreground on background is 9.578:1; accent background with foreground is 4.754:1. Task or brand colors override these. Apply tokens only to new elements, and verify contrast over the actual glass, since opaque checks do not validate translucent surfaces.
motionAndInteraction: Explicit: droplets, lenses, or flexible panels animate, with deformation continuous with refraction. Video is driven from seekable composition time, and live pointer, hover, or scroll input applies only to interactive delivery. Suggested HTML route: deterministic focus or pointer nudges with a static image fallback for reduced motion. Easing, tempo, and speed are unspecified.
audio: Audio direction is unspecified in the source for this style. Inferred: because the effect is optical, sound should be chosen from the topic and audience, with restraint as a suggestion only. No fixed music, voiceover, or sound effect is required. A voice-card pattern is optional and needs real audio content.
assetRequirements: A recognizable background visible through the glass is required, but no assets are supplied, so specific assets are unspecified. 3D route: Three.js transmission via MeshPhysicalMaterial (transmission, ior, roughness) with an offscreen background render target that must not be sampled in a feedback loop. 2D route: labeled screen-space or SVG displacement. Load fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulations.
combinations: Liquid Glass alone suits hero refraction moments. Hybrid with style-114 (metaball droplets): refraction derives from the same surface, dispersion stays minimal, and text never sits behind refraction. Hybrid with style-096 (product pacing): one glass element per shot, with text outside it. Motion references: motion-014 orb for bounded deformation, motion-021 orbit (lists Liquid Glass as good fit; requires real 3D depth), and motion-011 voice card only with real audio. A separate compatibility block lists flat vector, collage, and editorial fits that do not match this optical style; treat it as unverified.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary composition and export pipeline, using data-composition-id, a paused GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines, and the check, snapshot, and render commands. Remotion is a fallback only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. Three.js and the style renderer own visuals, GSAP owns motion, and chroma-js only validates colors. Inspect opening, action, transition, and closing frames plus audio sync and loop continuity before delivery. Physical fluid accuracy is not claimed.
